items.stem: What logs first: a `Promise.resolve().then(...)` callback or a `setTimeout(..., 0)` callback scheduled just before it?

options.text: The promise callback, because microtasks run before the next macrotask
options.rationale: Correct: the microtask queue drains before the next macrotask (timer) callback.

options.text: The setTimeout callback, because 0ms means immediate
options.rationale: Timer callbacks are macrotasks and run after microtasks.

options.text: They always log in source order
options.rationale: Queue type, not source order, decides timing here.

items.explanation: Correct: the microtask queue drains before the next macrotask (timer) callback.

items.stem: Which TWO are correct about arrow functions and this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An arrow function uses this from its enclosing lexical scope
options.rationale: Correct: arrow functions do not bind their own this.

options.text: bind has no effect on an arrow function's this
options.rationale: Correct: you cannot rebind an arrow function's this.

options.text: Arrow functions get a fresh this per call
options.rationale: They do not have their own this.
Arrow functions cannot be used as constructors.

items.explanation: Correct: arrow functions do not bind their own this.

items.stem: You need to cancel an in-flight fetch when the user navigates away. Which tool fits?

options.text: An AbortController whose signal is passed to fetch
options.rationale: Correct: AbortController cancels the fetch via its signal.
fetch is not a timer; clearTimeout does not cancel it.
Nulling the reference does not abort the request.
try/catch handles errors but does not cancel the request.

items.explanation: Correct: AbortController cancels the fetch via its signal.
